issues.legal_issue: A subsequent criminal prosecution is barred when the accused has already been acquitted after trial and the later prosecution rests on the same factual substratum.
material_facts: The earlier prosecution alleged that the accused forged a power of attorney and used it to sell the complainant’s land; the accused was acquitted, and that acquittal was undisputed.
The later FIR again concerned the same power of attorney and land sales, although it added allegations and charges, including impersonation and collusion.
The complainant had also brought a civil suit seeking cancellation of the same power of attorney.
The later FIR did not disclose the earlier acquittal or the civil suit.
issues.conclusion: The later prosecution was unsustainable because it concerned the same factual substratum as the prosecution that had ended in acquittal. The FIR and the orders rejecting discharge and affirming that rejection were set aside, and the appeal was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 300(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure bars a person who has been tried by a court of competent jurisdiction and acquitted, while the acquittal remains in force, from being tried again for the same offence or, on the same facts, for another offence for which a different charge could have been made or a conviction could have been entered under Section 221(1) or (2) CrPC. Where the factual substratum is the same, adding offence sections does not by itself make the later prosecution distinct. The judgment relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.subsequent_criminal_prosecution: A later criminal prosecution was initiated against the accused after an earlier prosecution concerning the alleged conduct.
predicates.prior_competent_trial_acquittal: A court of competent jurisdiction had tried the accused and acquitted them, and the acquittal remained in force.
predicates.same_factual_substratum: The later prosecution relied on the same essential alleged conduct and transactions as the earlier prosecution, even if it added allegations or offence labels.

issues.definition: When a later criminal prosecution follows an acquittal and rests on the same essential alleged conduct, the later prosecution is unsustainable.
